pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: The Telegram
work.note: A referência é o telegrama que traz notícias: Have you heard…?. Em 24 de maio de 1844, Samuel Morse enviou de Washington a Baltimore a mensagem 'What hath God wrought', primeira transmissão pública de longa distância pelo telégrafo elétrico nos Estados Unidos. O contexto da obra ajuda o estudante a usar dar notícias: Have you heard the news? Guess what! I won a prize. Did you hear what happened? em uma situação concr

facts.label: Boas notícias e planos
facts.sub: Use o passado para a notícia: I passed my exam! Use going to para planos: I’m going to celebrate. Use I’ll para oferecer: I’ll bring a cake.

facts.label: Notícias
facts.sub: Para contar uma boa notícia, use o passado simples: I passed my exam! I won a prize. Depois diga o sentimento: I’m so happy. Para responder, diga Congratulations! ou I’m so proud of you.

facts.label: Planos
facts.sub: Para falar de planos, use am/is/are going to: I’m going to celebrate with my family. Are you going to come? Use tonight, tomorrow ou this weekend para dar o tempo.

answers: “Congratulations” is for good news. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I’m going celebrate”. → Falso (We say I’m going to celebrate.)
“I’ll bring a cake” is an offer. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A sunny cafe · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Friday afternoon in a sunny cafe in Perth. Warm light fills the room. Liam sits near the window with a coffee. His friend Nina comes in with a big smile. She holds a letter in her hand. Liam asks about the news.
“Nina! You look so happy! What’s the news?” says Liam. “I passed my exam! The result came this morning.” says Nina. “Great! I’m so proud of you.” says Liam.
